verses.1:1: The burden of the Lord's word to Israel through the hand of Malachi.
verses.1:2: "I have loved you," says the Lord, "and you have said, 'In what way have You loved us?' Was Esau not Jacob's brother?" says the Lord. "Yet I have loved Jacob,
verses.1:3: but Esau I have hated, and I have turned his mountains into a wasteland, and his inheritance over to the dragons of the desert."
verses.1:4: And if Edom says, "We have been destroyed, yet returning we will rebuild what has been destroyed," this is what the Lord of hosts says: "They will build, and I will destroy; and they will be called the borders of wickedness, and the people with whom the Lord is angry forever."
verses.1:5: And your eyes will see, and you will say, "May the Lord be magnified beyond the border of Israel."
verses.1:6: "A son honors his father, and a servant his master. If then I am a father, where is My honor? And if I am the Lord, where is the fear of Me?" says the Lord of hosts. "To you, priests, who despise My name! And you have said, 'In what way have we despised Your name?'
verses.1:7: You offer polluted bread on My altar, and you say, 'In what way have we polluted You?' In saying, 'The table of the Lord is despised.'
verses.1:8: If you offer what is blind for sacrifice, is it not evil? And if you offer what is lame and sick, is it not evil? Offer it to your governor; see if it will please him, or if he will accept your face," says the Lord of hosts.
verses.1:9: "And now implore the face of God, that He may have mercy on you (for from your hand this has been done), if in any way He may accept your faces," says the Lord of hosts.
verses.1:10: "Who is there among you who would shut the doors and kindle My altar for nothing? I have no pleasure in you," says the Lord of hosts, "and I will not accept a gift from your hand.
verses.1:11: For from the rising of the sun even to its setting, My name is great among the nations, and in every place sacrifice is made, and a pure offering is offered to My name; for My name is great among the nations," says the Lord of hosts.
verses.1:12: "And you have polluted it in saying, 'The table of the Lord is defiled, and what is placed on it is contemptible, along with the fire that devours it.'
verses.1:13: And you have said, 'Look, out of weariness!' and you have snorted at it," says the Lord of hosts. "And you have brought in from plunder what is lame and sick, and you have brought in a gift. Will I accept it from your hand?" says the Lord.
verses.1:14: "Cursed is the deceiver who has a male in his flock, and making a vow sacrifices what is weak to the Lord; for I am a great king," says the Lord of hosts, "and My name is fearsome among the nations."
verses.2:1: "And now this command is to you, priests.
verses.2:2: If you will not listen, and if you will not lay it to heart, so as to give glory to My name," says the Lord of hosts, "I will send poverty upon you, and I will curse your blessings, and I will curse them, because you have not laid it to heart.
verses.2:3: Look, I will cast away your arm, and I will scatter over your faces the dung of your solemn feasts, and it will take you away with it.
verses.2:4: And you will know that I have sent this command to you, so that My covenant might be with Levi," says the Lord of hosts.
verses.2:5: "My covenant with him was of life and peace, and I gave him fear, and he feared Me, and before the face of My name he trembled.
verses.2:6: The law of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found on his lips; in peace and in equity he walked with Me, and he turned many away from iniquity.
verses.2:7: For the lips of a priest will guard knowledge, and they will seek the law from his mouth, for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.
verses.2:8: But you have departed from the way, and you have caused very many to stumble in the law; you have made the covenant of Levi void," says the Lord of hosts.
verses.2:9: "Therefore I also have made you contemptible and lowly before all the peoples, just as you have not kept My ways, and have shown partiality in the law."
verses.2:10: Is there not one father of us all? Has not one God created us? Why then does each one of us despise his brother, violating the covenant of our fathers?
verses.2:11: Judah has transgressed, and an abomination has been committed in Israel and in Jerusalem, for Judah has defiled the holiness of the Lord, which He loved, and has married the daughter of a foreign god.
verses.2:12: The Lord will destroy the man who does this, master and disciple, from the tents of Jacob, and him who offers a gift to the Lord of hosts.
verses.2:13: "And this you have done again: you were covering the altar of the Lord with tears, with weeping and groaning, so that I no longer look toward the sacrifice, nor accept anything pleasing from your hand."
verses.2:14: And you have said, "For what reason?" Because the Lord has borne witness between you and the wife of your youth, whom you have despised; and yet she is your partner, and the wife of your covenant.
verses.2:15: Did not One make them, and the remnant of the spirit is His? And what does the One seek, except the seed of God? Guard your spirit therefore, and do not despise the wife of your youth.
verses.2:16: "When you hate her, send her away," says the Lord God of Israel, "yet iniquity will cover his garment," says the Lord of hosts. "Guard your spirit, and do not despise her."
verses.2:17: You have made the Lord weary with your words, and you have said, "In what way have we made Him weary?" In saying, "Everyone who does evil is good in the sight of the Lord, and such ones please Him; or else, where is the God of judgment?"
verses.3:1: "Look, I am sending My messenger, and he will prepare the way before My face; and at once the Sovereign whom you seek will come to His temple, and the messenger of the covenant whom you desire. Look, He is coming," says the Lord of hosts.
verses.3:2: And who will be able to think of the day of His coming, and who will stand to see Him? For He Himself is like a smelting fire, and like the herb of fullers;
verses.3:3: and He will sit smelting and cleansing silver, and He will purify the sons of Levi, and He will refine them like gold and like silver, and they will be the Lord's, offering sacrifices in righteousness.
verses.3:4: And the sacrifice of Judah and Jerusalem will please the Lord, as in the days of old, and as in the ancient years.
verses.3:5: "And I will draw near to you in judgment, and I will be a swift witness against sorcerers, and adulterers, and perjurers, and against those who defraud the hired worker of his wage, and widows and orphans, and oppress the foreigner, and have not feared Me," says the Lord of hosts.
verses.3:6: "For I am the Lord, and I do not change; and you, sons of Jacob, have not been consumed.
verses.3:7: For from the days of your fathers you have departed from My statutes, and have not kept them. Return to Me, and I will return to you," says the Lord of hosts. "And you have said, 'In what way will we return?'
verses.3:8: Will a man afflict God, that you are piercing Me? And you have said, 'In what way are we piercing You?' In tithes and in firstfruits.
verses.3:9: And in scarcity you are cursed, and you are piercing Me, the whole nation.
verses.3:10: Bring the whole tithe into the storehouse, and let there be food in My house; and test Me in this," says the Lord, "if I will not open for you the floodgates of heaven, and pour out for you a blessing even to abundance,
verses.3:11: and I will rebuke the devourer for your sake, and it will not ruin the fruit of your land, nor will the vine in the field be barren," says the Lord of hosts.
verses.3:12: "And all nations will call you blessed, for you will be a desirable land," says the Lord of hosts.
verses.3:13: "Your words have grown strong against Me," says the Lord.
verses.3:14: "And you have said, 'What have we spoken against You?' You have said, 'Fruitless is the one who serves God; and what profit is there because we have kept His precepts, and because we have walked sorrowfully before the Lord of hosts?
verses.3:15: Therefore now we call the arrogant blessed, since those who do wickedness have been built up, and they have put God to the test, and have been kept safe.'"
verses.3:16: Then those who feared the Lord spoke, each one with his neighbor; and the Lord paid attention and heard, and a book of remembrance was written before Him for those who fear the Lord and think on His name.
verses.3:17: "And they will be Mine," says the Lord of hosts, "on the day when I act, for a special possession; and I will spare them, just as a man spares his son who serves him.
verses.3:18: And you will turn back, and you will see what is between the righteous and the wicked, and between the one who serves God and the one who does not serve Him."
verses.4:1: "For look, the day will come, burning like a furnace; and all the proud and all who do wickedness will be stubble; and the coming day will set them ablaze," says the Lord of hosts, "which will not leave them root or sprout.
verses.4:2: And for you who fear My name, the sun of righteousness will rise, and healing in its wings; and you will go out and leap like calves from the herd.
verses.4:3: And you will trample the wicked, when they become ashes under the sole of your feet, on the day when I act," says the Lord of hosts.
verses.4:4: "Remember the law of Moses My servant, which I commanded him at Horeb for all Israel, precepts and judgments.
verses.4:5: Look, I will send you Elijah the prophet, before the great and fearsome day of the Lord comes.
verses.4:6: And he will turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, or else I might come and strike the land with a curse."

notes.1:3: Vulgate reads "dragons of the desert" (dracones deserti), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text refers to "jackals of the wilderness."
notes.1:8: The Latin idiom "accept your face" (suscipere faciem, repeated in 1:9; cf. 2:9) mirrors Hebrew usage meaning to receive someone with favor or show partiality.
notes.1:10: Vulgate frames this as a rhetorical rebuke of mercenary priests ("who would shut the doors and kindle My altar for nothing," gratuito), whereas the Hebrew expresses a wish that someone would shut the doors so they would not kindle the altar in vain.
notes.1:11: Vulgate uses present-tense verbs ("is great," "sacrifice is made," "is offered") and renders the Hebrew "incense is burned" more broadly as "sacrifice is made" (sacrificatur).
notes.1:12: Vulgate reads "what is placed on it is contemptible, along with the fire that devours it," differing from the Hebrew text's "its fruit, its food."
notes.2:2: Vulgate reads "poverty" (egestatem) where the Hebrew has "the curse," and translates both curses in the future tense ("I will curse... and I will curse them") rather than shifting to a completed past tense.
notes.2:3: Literally "I will cast away the arm for you" (projiciam vobis brachium); the Vulgate reads the Hebrew consonants as "arm" rather than "seed/offspring" and renders "cast away" instead of "rebuke."
notes.2:12: Vulgate renders the difficult Hebrew idiom (literally "one who wakes and one who answers") as "master and disciple" (magistrum et discipulum).
notes.2:15: The grammar is notoriously difficult; the Vulgate literally asks "Did not One make [them], and the remnant of the spirit is His?" leaving the object of "make" (fecit) unexpressed. Capitalization of 'One'/'His' takes unus as referring to God (rather than Adam/Abraham or the married couple); subject to edition-wide policy.
notes.2:16: Vulgate reads a second-person directive ("When you hate her, send her away," cf. Deut 24:1) followed by the warning that "iniquity will cover his garment"; the Hebrew opening clause can also be read as "he hates sending away."
notes.3:1: Clem1598-USFX prints capitalized Dominator ('the Sovereign'); capitalization of 'Sovereign', 'His', and 'He' (versus lowercase 'he' for My messenger) is subject to edition-wide policy.
notes.3:2: Vulgate reads "think of the day of His coming" (cogitare) and "to see Him" (ad videndum eum), where the Hebrew has "endure the day of His coming" and "when He appears"; "herb of fullers" (herba fullonum) refers to an alkali plant used in laundering cloth.
notes.3:8: Vulgate translates the Hebrew verb for "rob/defraud" with "afflict" (affliget) and "pierce" (configitis, also in 3:9), reads "firstfruits" (primitiis) for Hebrew "contributions," and in 3:9 reads "in scarcity" (in penuria, cf. 2:2) where the Hebrew has "with a curse."
notes.4:1: In native Clementine Vulgate numbering (Clem1598-USFX), chapter 4 comprises 4:1-6 (mapped to Saints.Bible 3:19-24, where 4:4 = Saints 3:24 and 4:5-6 = Saints 3:22-23).
notes.4:2: Vulgate reads "from the herd" (de armento), whereas the Hebrew has "from the stall."
notes.4:4: In native Clementine Vulgate order (matching the Hebrew MT), the charge to remember the law of Moses stands at 4:4 before the Elijah prophecy in 4:5-6 (whereas Saints.Bible places Moses at 3:24 after Elijah at 3:22-23).
notes.4:5: Native Clementine Vulgate 4:5-6 place the Elijah prophecy after 4:4 (mapped to Saints.Bible 3:22-23, which place Elijah before Moses at 3:24); in 4:6 "curse" translates anathemate, a ban of utter destruction.
